blocks.text: After the Sui-Tang Grand Canal was completed, Jiangnan’s economy and culture thrived. Scholars such as Bai Juyi shaped the iconic image of Jiangnan through poetry, making its aesthetic widely known. During the Ming and Qing dynasties, the water towns we see today, including Zhouzhuang, Wuzhen and Tongli, reached their full prosperity.

Jiangnan water towns carry soft, timeless beauty. Mist and drizzling rain wrap around serene waterways, with stone arch bridges, bluestone paths, waterside houses and quiet docks. Wupeng (乌篷) black-awning boats, willows, oil-paper umbrellas, bamboo crafts, celadon, folding fans and pottery add to the simple and elegant Jiangnan style.

Needs Work. Su‑style architecture takes private yuanlin (园林) gardens as its representative, so more research should be done about the folk dwellings seen in Jiangnan water towns. Local Su-style architecture (苏派建筑) are defined by white walls, black tiles, graceful upturned eaves, huachuang (花窗) windows, and small courtyards.
